subject: LedgerPay evaluation recap — suggested open-model vs baseline plan
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@ledgerpay.com>, Priya Anand <priya@ledgerpay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T14:12:00Z
Subject: LedgerPay evaluation recap — suggested open-model vs baseline plan

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call today — quick recap and recommended next steps so we can move the trial forward. High-level points below, followed by concrete asks.

Call summary:
- Goal: automate invoice reconciliation comments + generate humanized explanations for exceptions (customer-facing).
- Primary constraints you mentioned: 1) strict PII redaction, 2) 300ms target p95 latency on short inference paths, 3) cost target ~40% below your current baseline per-inference.

Model-fit summary and recommendation:
- We recommend evaluating an open model variant first (LLaMA-3-13B quantized q4o) against your current proprietary baseline (internal reference: redwood-1-small-baseline). Preliminary local benchmarks (attached summary) show parity on correctness metrics for structured extraction prompts within ~3–6% absolute, with lower cost.
- Acceptance threshold proposal: for the LedgerPay use case, a model passes parity if it meets both: (a) semantic accuracy (F1) within 5% of baseline on the verification prompt set, and (b) no user-facing regression as measured by our human eval rubric (clarity >= 4/5 on a 50-sample canary set).

Quality regression concerns and mitigations:
- Risk: generation verbosity and hallucination on rare vendor abbreviations. Mitigation: add targeted prompt anchors and a small retrieval layer for vendor catalogs (we included a curated prompt set that exercises those edge cases).
- Canary rollout: canary on 5% of live traffic with automatic rollback if hallucination rate increases >2x or human-eval score drops below threshold.

Operational notes (latency & cost):
- LLaMA-3-13B q4o estimated p95 latency: 220–300ms on our Dedicated 1xA100 equivalent (with KV cache warm). Cost estimate: ~0.6x your current per-call compute when batched for reconciliation jobs.

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm you want LLaMA-3-13B q4o as the initial open-model candidate (or tell us if you prefer trying a 7B variant first).
2) Approve access to a small sample of production logs (PII redacted) so we can run the acceptance prompt set against your baseline and the candidate.
3) If agreed, we’ll provision a 14-day trial: evaluation harness + canary config + weekly syncs. Proposed SOW attached.

Attachments: ledgerpay_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt coverage + canary set), parity_bench_results_summary.csv (prelim local run), proposed_trial_sow.docx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to lock timelines.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Camila — useful recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we sign off on the trial:

1) Latency: you cite 220–300ms p95 — is that for single-request inference (no batching) or an amortized figure when doing micro-batches? Our production path is very latency sensitive and we can’t buffer.
2) Cost: do you have a rough $$ per-1k-inferences for the open-model candidate vs our baseline? Even a back-of-envelope helps with procurement.

Also, curious about the human-eval threshold you mentioned (clarity >= 4/5). What sample size and rubric do you use? If we move forward we’ll need that documented for the security/compliance review.

On the sample logs: we can provide a redacted dump by Friday; will that be enough for your harness?

—Jordan

Jordan — quick technical answers and config suggestions from infra/SE: 

1) Latency: the 220–300ms p95 number I quoted is for single-request inference (no batching) with KV cache warm and using our Dedicated GPU profile (1xA100 equiv). For cold start on rarely-seen vendor contexts expect +40–80ms.

2) Cost estimate: rough compute-only delta: open-model (LLaMA-3-13B q4o) ~ $0.045 per inference, redwood-1-small-baseline ~ $0.08 per inference when both are tuned for your prompt lengths — these are compute-only proxy numbers; total bill will include egress and service fees. Procurement should expect ~45–55% compute delta.

3) Human-eval rubric + sample size: Marissa (cc'd) ran a 50-sample blinded eval across the reconciliation prompt set: dimensions were Accuracy (binary), Clarity (1–5 Likert), and Hallucination flag (Y/N). We recommend the 50-sample canary initially; if LedgerPay prefers, we can expand to 200 samples for stronger statistical power.

4) Recommended runtime config for trial: KV cache enabled, response-length cap = 256 tokens, micro-batch disabled for the low-latency path, and per-request timeout = 1s. Use q4o quantization with act-order disabled (best observed for this workload).

5) Fallback policy: if canary metrics breach thresholds, traffic will fail-over to your baseline (redwood-1-small-baseline) automatically.

I can produce a short runnable checklist for your SRE team — would you prefer a runnable Terraform snippet + runtime YAML or just a checklist doc?

—Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
